question: Which of the following edicts of King Ashoka describes the Kalinga war?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rock Edict - XIII**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The great **Emperor Ashoka, the third monarch of the Maurya dynasty** converted to Buddhism after witnessing the horrific effects of war in Kalinga.
 
• The **Kalinga war is described in Rock Edict XIII of King Ashoka**.
 
• The edict is written in** Pali on a large rock in the Dhauli Hills, near the site of the w**ar.
 
• He **erected pillars and edicts** all over the subcontinent and even in modern-day Afghanistan, Nepal, Bangladesh and Pakistan to spread the Buddha’s word.
 
• **James Prinsep,** a British antiquary and colonial administrator was the** first person to decipher Ashoka’s edicts.**
 
• There are **33 inscriptions** in total and are primarily classified into the following:
 
 
• Major rock edicts
 
• Minor rock edicts
 
• Separate rock edicts
 
• Major pillar edicts 
 
• Minor pillar edicts
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rock Edict - II** mentions the **Medical treatment of humans and animals, the planting of fruits, and medicinal herbs and the digging of wells.**
 
• Mentions the Pandyas, Satyapuras and Keralaputras of South India.
 
• **Rock Edict - XI** mentions** Dhamma is the best policy to follow, **which includes **respect for elders and concern for slaves and servants.**
 
• **Rock Edict - XII** mentions** an appeal for developing tolerance towards all religious sects.**
 
• The direct and immediate effect of the Kalinga war was the **conversion of Ashoka to Buddhism.**
